title: Compact assurance checkflow + pricing sensitivity pilot
creator: Ethan Park
description:
Goal: build a lightweight, tiered security-questionnaire onramp that reduces evidence burden for low-risk customers while enabling tiered pricing credits for verified attestations.

Scope: prototype a compact checkflow (10–12 canonical items mapped from CAIQ), a risk-weighted scoring engine, and a pricing-credit simulator. Component pieces: compact questionnaire UI, mapping layer to CAIQ artifacts, automated evidence collector checklist, backend attestation token issuance, and an experiment to measure conversion and legal acceptance.

Why: enterprise prospects often abandon long questionnaires or request manual evidence, which slows contract velocity and burdens SE/Legal. A compact flow that surfaces only material controls + issues a verifiable attestation token can reduce time-to-yes and enable a pricing lever tied to attestation confidence.

Success metrics: 1) reduce average questionnaire completion time for Tier 1 customers by 60%, 2) increase onramp conversion (signed contract after first security pass) by 12%, 3) measure delta in support ticket volume for questionnaire handoffs, 4) validate pricing elasticity with >100 customers in A/B pilot.

Non-goals: full CAIQ export or replacing enterprise manual attestations for high-risk regulated customers. This is an onramp + pricing experiment for mid-market and fast-moving enterprise deals.
comments: 2025-02-11 - Kickoff: aligned with Sales and Solutions. Decided to limit compact flow to controls that cover data residency, access controls, encryption, and incident response. Legal asked to standardize attestation wording.

2025-02-18 - Design review: DES and PM reviewed two UI prototypes. Chosen pattern: progressive disclosure (compact summary + optional deep-dive). Design requested an 'evidence placeholder' to attach existing customer docs.

2025-02-22 - Eng sync: ENG team proposed risk-scoring function prototype using weighted CAIQ mapping; recommended backend token as signed JWT with claim schema (issuer, customer_id, score, timestamp, accepted_controls). ENG flagged need for KMS integration for signing keys.

2025-02-25 - Trade-off: can issue 'soft attestation' immediately with user-entered answers, but Legal prefers signed attestation only after minimal verification (automated checks + manual review for borderline scores). Decided to launch with soft attestation + explicit review step at score < threshold.

2025-03-02 - Experiment plan drafted: A/B groups (control = current process, variant = compact checkflow + pricing credit teaser). Metrics and dashboard are instrumented in Growth experiment board. Next: finalize pricing tiers and legal language for attestation token.
notes: Design decision: present potential pricing credit as a percent range (e.g., 5–15%) rather than fixed amount to avoid committing on legal-sensitive discounts. Engineering will return cost-to-serve delta for each score band by 2025-03-05.
risks: 1) Sales pushback on 'soft attestation' acceptance among enterprise buyers; 2) Legal compliance for attestation language; 3) KMS/HSM integration slippage could block signed token issuance; 4) Pricing experiment confounded by sales incentives. Mitigations: include manual escalation path, legal signoff checkpoint, and decouple experiment from quota crediting until validated.
next_steps: Finalize attestation claim schema and KMS signing plan (due 2025-03-05)
Design handoff assets for frontend: compact questionnaire + evidence placeholder components (DES deliverable)
Engineer prototype risk-scoring service and token generator (ENG task)
Draft experiment variant pricing bands and success thresholds with Growth/Finance
